info.name: CrawlRAG — Full API Collection
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for CrawlRAG v0.2.0.

End-to-end flow:
  1. Scrape website  (POST /scraping/scrape)
  2. Build RAG index (POST /rag/embed-all) — runs clean → chunk → embed in one call
  3. Check status    (GET  /rag/status)
  4. Search chunks   (POST /rag/search)
  5. Get LLM answer  (POST /rag/answer)

Models used:
  • Embeddings: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (384-dim, ~130 MB, high MTEB benchmark score)
  • LLM:        Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (~3 GB, instruction-tuned reasoning)

Base URL variable: {{base_url}} = http://127.0.0.1:8000

variable.description: Replace with an actual doc_id from the List Documents response

item.name: 1. Web Scraping
item.description: Step 1 of the pipeline. Crawl a website and save each page as a JSON file in data/scraped/.

request.description:
BFS recursive crawl from the seed URL.

What happens:
  1. Playwright renders JavaScript (React/Vue/Angular SPAs supported)
  2. BeautifulSoup extracts: title, headings (h1–h6), paragraphs, links
  3. Discovers all internal links and crawls each subpage
  4. Each page is saved as a separate JSON in data/scraped/
  5. Returns full data for every scraped page

Fields:
  url                  - Seed URL to start crawling from (required)
  max_depth            - BFS depth limit (0 = seed page only, 2 = seed + 2 levels deep)
  max_pages            - Hard cap on total pages scraped
  render_js            - true = use Playwright; false = fast HTTPX-only
  wait_seconds         - Time to wait after page load for JS hydration
  concurrency          - Parallel page workers
  delay_seconds        - Polite delay between requests
  stay_within_path     - Only crawl under the seed URL path
  crawl_external_links - Also follow external links found on pages
  force_refresh        - Re-scrape pages even if cached

Scrape a single static page quickly without JavaScript rendering.
Use max_depth=0, max_pages=1, render_js=false for maximum speed.

item.name: 3. RAG Pipeline — Step by Step
item.description:
Individual pipeline stages for fine-grained control.

ORDER: clean → chunk → embed → search/answer

TIP: Use 'RAG Pipeline — One-Shot (Recommended)' folder to run the full pipeline in a single call instead.

request.description:
Clean raw scraped JSON and write cleaned output to data/clean_data/.

What it removes: cookie banners, nav menus, tracking scripts, excessive whitespace.
What it preserves: headings, contact info (+91 phone, email, address), prices, product data.

doc_id: null = clean all documents; "doc_abc123" = clean only that document.
min_paragraph_length: text blocks shorter than this are dropped (noise filter).
Batch-clean all stored scraped documents in one operation.

Split cleaned documents into overlapping semantic chunks using Recursive Character Chunking.

Algorithm splits text hierarchically by: \n\n → \n → ". " → " " → character
This respects natural sentence and paragraph boundaries.

chunk_size: max characters per chunk (default: 400)
chunk_overlap: characters shared between adjacent chunks (default: 80)
  → Overlap prevents context loss at chunk boundaries.

Output saved to: data/chunked_data/{doc_id}_chunks.json
Clean and chunk ALL scraped documents in one combined batch. No body required.

Generate 384-dim L2-normalised embeddings using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and add them to the vector store.

First call downloads the model (~90 MB) to models/embeddings/. Subsequent calls use the local cache.

batch_size: how many texts are embedded per GPU/CPU batch. Higher = faster but more RAM.
doc_id: null = embed all chunked documents; "doc_abc123" = embed only that document.

Vector store: data/vector_store/vector_index.npy + metadata.json

item.name: 4. RAG Pipeline — One-Shot (Recommended) ⭐
item.description:
Runs the complete pipeline (clean → chunk → embed → store) in a single API call.
Use this instead of running Steps A, B, C individually.

request.description:
ONE CALL to run the entire RAG ingestion pipeline:
  1. Clean all scraped documents (remove boilerplate)
  2. Chunk all cleaned text (400-char chunks, 80-char overlap)
  3. Generate embeddings with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim)
  4. Clear old index and store new vectors

Run this after every scrape to rebuild the knowledge base.

Response includes:
  indexed_vector_count - total chunk vectors stored
  elapsed_seconds      - total time taken

item.name: 5. Search & Answer
item.description:
Query the vector store and get grounded LLM answers.

Pre-requisite: Run 'embed-all' first to build the index.

request.description:
Check all pipeline stage counts and model cache status before querying.

Expected response:
{
  "scraped_document_count": 45,
  "cleaned_document_count": 45,
  "chunked_document_count": 45,
  "vector_count": 1240,
  "embedding_dimension": 384,
  "embedding_model": "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
  "embedding_model_cached_locally": true,
  "llm_model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
  "llm_model_cached_locally": true,
  "vector_store_stats": { ... }
}

vector_count > 0 means the index is ready for search/answer.

body.raw:
{
  "query": "what books are available in mystery category",
  "top_k": 7,
  "score_threshold": 0.2,
  "reframe": false,
  "temperature": 0.1
}

request.description:
Hybrid semantic + keyword search over the vector store. Returns the top-K most relevant text chunks.

Retrieval strategy:
  1. Dense: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine similarity (primary)
  2. Sparse: phrase + keyword boost on chunk text and title
  3. Contact intent boost: +score when query contains contact/phone/address keywords
  4. Optional: LLM reframing (set reframe: true) for improved recall on vague queries

Fields:
  query           - Natural language search query (also accepts: question, prompt, q, input, text)
  top_k           - Max results to return (1–50, default: 7)
  score_threshold - Min hybrid score to include (0.0–1.0, default: 0.2). Lower = more results.
  reframe         - LLM rewrites query for better retrieval (false = faster)
  temperature     - LLM temperature for reframing (default: 0.1)

Response: array of SearchResultItem with chunk_id, url, title, text, score, chunk_index
Contact-intent queries get an automatic keyword boost for chunks containing phone numbers, addresses, and email addresses. Use a lower score_threshold (0.1) when searching for specific entities.

body.raw:
{
  "query": "Tell me about Lab Girl book — its price, category and availability",
  "top_k": 7,
  "score_threshold": 0.2,
  "reframe": true,
  "temperature": 0.1,
  "max_new_tokens": 512
}

request.description:
Retrieves relevant context chunks and generates a grounded, factual answer using the local Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct LLM.

Pipeline inside this endpoint:
  1. Embed query with all-MiniLM-L6-v2
  2. [Optional] Reframe query with LLM for better recall
  3. Hybrid search: cosine similarity + keyword boost
  4. Deduplicate retrieved chunks by chunk_id
  5. Build context: Source[1] ... Source[N]
  6. Generate answer: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (max_new_tokens=512, temp=0.1)
  7. Post-process: LLMOutputCleaner strips robotic meta-commentary

Query aliases: also accepts 'question', 'prompt', 'q', 'input', 'text' instead of 'query'.

Response:
{
  "query": "...",
  "answer": "Lab Girl is a memoir by Hope Jahren priced at £45.17...",
  "sources": [ { "chunk_id": "...", "title": "...", "score": 0.91, ... } ],
  "sources_count": 3
}

body.raw:
{
  "question": "What services does this company offer?",
  "top_k": 7,
  "score_threshold": 0.2,
  "reframe": true,
  "temperature": 0.1,
  "max_new_tokens": 512
}

request.description: Demonstrates the QueryNormalizerMixin: the 'question' field is automatically mapped to 'query' before validation. Also accepts: prompt, q, input, text.

item.name: RAG Answer — With Query Reframing (Best Accuracy)

request.description:
For short or vague queries, set reframe: true. The LLM expands 'best book' into more precise retrieval keywords before embedding, improving recall.

Also use a slightly lower score_threshold (0.15) for short queries.
